subtopics.keyConceptSummary: Ghanaian society has long been shaped by socio-cultural practices such as inheritance and succession patterns, the structure of the family system, and rites of passage like naming ceremonies and puberty rites. These practices have influenced how people relate to their identity and community.

subtopics.title: Colonialism and Nationalism

subtopics.keyConceptSummary: British colonial rule in Ghana (1874-1957) was met with resistance from traditional leaders and, later, organised nationalist movements such as the UGCC and CPP. Key events, including the 1948 Riots and the arrest of the Big Six, paved the way to independence in 1957, with women playing a notable role throughout the struggle.
